$comment: Reviewer pool for /adversarial-review (HARNESS-071, #955).
Ordered allow-list of models permitted to SIGN a review.md. Since HARNESS-093 the
launcher DRAWS one member at random; the whole array is the gate's allow-list, which
dotf spec archive enforces via checkReviewGate.
Standing rule (amended 2026-10-09, #1923, amendment B): an Anthropic model never
signs an adversarial review ALONE. The reviewer must not be the implementer, and
Claude implements nearly every change in this repo — BUG-074 was reviewed twice
by claude-opus-5 before anyone noticed, which is the incident this file exists to
prevent. So every signed review keeps a first signature from another vendor, and
an Anthropic member signs only as `signs: second` (a second signature beside a
first signer of another vendor) or `signs: fallback` (in place of the first
signers when they failed for a classified reason the launch request records).
`dotf spec archive` enforces it: pool loading refuses an Anthropic member that
would sign first, and the gate checks roles, reason and that the vendors differ.
Second signature: required when proposal.md declares `risk: high`. Only Sonnet
declares `signs: second` today, so a high-risk spec's second signature depends on
the Anthropic review key; when it is down, wait, or waive or lower the risk in
proposal.md with a stated reason. That dependency is deliberate (the owner wants
the quality tier in play, 2026-10-09) and costs about 8 reviews a month.
`vendor` is who trains the model: the unit the second signature must differ in.
`signs` defaults to `first`.
PR-Agent reads this file too (AI-045 AC9, #1923): each `pr_agent` block is that
member's PR-Agent model, its weight in the CI draw, and its reasoning effort.
`route: risk` is not drawn: it reviews first when a PR crosses `pr_agent_risk`
(changed lines, or the label). `dotf pr route` holds the allowlist of
Anthropic models CI may spend on, so an edit here cannot route CI onto another.
Entries are model IDS, not tool names, and that distinction is load-bearing:
`agy` also serves claude-opus-4-6-thinking and claude-sonnet-4-6, so pinning
the tool would guarantee nothing. Pinning the id does.
`id` is the canonical string a reviewer records in review.md and the gate
matches on. `provider`/`model` are the launcher's flags, kept explicit rather
than parsed out of `id`: BUG-074 round 3 ran on the right model only because
~/.pi/agent/settings.json on one machine happened to default to it — pi's own
default provider is google, and that file is unversioned per-machine state.
A pin that depends on a default is not a pin.
Reasoning-class only. The latency-optimised daily models (nan/qwen3.6,
nan/gemma4) are deliberately absent: a reviewer that PASSes cheaply is worse
than no gate, because it converts the gate into a green checkmark. This file
is read once per spec, so slow is fine. A member is admitted by the bar, not
by its tier name: gemini-4-argon-high is in because it found the planted defect
on that bar (2026-11-14, #3471), as gemini-3.8-flash-high had when agy dropped
its Pro tier (owner decision 2026-10-14, #2385). gpt-oss-120b-medium is out
because it missed it twice; never admit it.
This is the load-bearing slice of H-044, not a replacement for it. H-044's
model-map.json maps a neutral tier (top|mid|low) to a provider per agent — a
different shape. Kept in a separate file so H-044 need not migrate this one.

Order is provenance, not precedence, since HARNESS-093 (#1370): the launcher draws one first-signer member at random (an Anthropic member is never drawn first), so every first signer is exercised in the ordinary course of reviews and NaN's per-model concurrency buckets are spread; --reviewer names one deliberately, which is how a run is reproduced. The roles below record why each member was admitted, not who runs first.

On saturation, measured 2026-08-20: NaN's concurrency limit is PER MODEL, not per API key (8 concurrent to deepseek gives 5x200 + 3x429, while mimo answers 200 during that saturation). So a spec review launched while the PR reviewer is saturating deepseek WILL fail, and falling through to another entry is the correct response rather than a bug. Do not 'fix' that by promoting the NaN sibling above the provider-diverse entry — it would trade an outage-proof fallback for a saturation-proof one and lose the stronger property. This file is read once per spec, so slow is fine; that is why availability does not outrank independence here.

pool.why: 1M context and a mandatory reasoning chain — roughly 4x slower than qwen3.6 on trivial prompts, which is the correct trade for a gate that runs once per spec. Exercised: BUG-074 round 3 re-ran the mutation battery itself rather than trusting the spec's table. Under the `dotf spec review` harness it completes where a quota death leaves nothing: kubelab OPS-024 (2026-09-05, #1511), a full FAIL review with three Majors, minutes after another member died on its quota; BUG-168 (2026-11-11), PASS with both of the spec's mutations reproduced.

A second provider family, independent of both NaN and Anthropic — provider diversity rather than merely a different model. Gemini 4 Argon at high effort, the Pro slot of the Gemini 4 family, admitted 2026-11-14 on the bar every member clears: the planted `((count++))` defect under `set -e` with count=0 (agy 1.5.8, macOS). It found the defect in 50 s, named the failing input (the first matching file) and gave the fix; the run is recorded on #3471. gemini-4-hydrogen-high passed the same bar in 66 s and is the measured replacement if this id is withdrawn; the arm keeps one agy member so its draw weight does not double while #3361 is open. History: this arm held gemini-3.1-pro-high until agy stopped serving it (roughly one random draw in five died at startup), then gemini-3.8-flash-high from 2026-10-14 by owner decision (#2385), marked PROVISIONAL until Gemini shipped a stronger model; no active spec carries a review signed by that id (checked 2026-11-14). gpt-oss-120b-medium, the only other non-Anthropic id agy serves, missed the bar twice and must not be admitted. When Gemini ships again, measure the new ids on the same bar before touching this entry. agy has no --provider flag; the model id selects the family. AUTH IS LOGIN, not a key (#1156): agy holds an OAuth token at ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/google_credentials.json and answers with no API key in the environment at all (measured 2026-08-22). This entry previously named GEMINI_API_KEY, a secret the registry has never declared, so every attempt to use the provider-diverse arm died at `dotf secrets run --only` -- and nothing noticed, because the primary always answered. The arm this pool exists to provide had therefore never run once.
pool.operational_note: The stall below was observed on gemini-3.8-flash-high, this arm's id until 2026-11-14, and is kept as the arm's history; whether gemini-4-argon-high stalls the same way is not yet known (the admission bar in `why` is a 50 s single-prompt run, not a full review). Stalls. Both of this arm's draws on AI-055 (2026-11-12; rounds 1 and 3 of that spec's four review rounds) stopped inside a `run_command` about 25 minutes into tool use and signed nothing. `nan/glm5.3-flash` took the other two rounds and completed both — round 2 as a FAIL verdict, round 4 as PASS, launched with `--reviewer` rather than a random draw so that a verdict existed at all. A stall is a refusal, not a pass: it signs nothing, and the provisional `review-round3.md` it leaves behind is deleted rather than committed so a later session cannot mistake it for a live verdict (AI-055 verification). Nothing about weight or admission changes here — the arm answers its probe and this is one spec. When it is drawn and stalls, relaunch with `--reviewer` naming a member that completed, or raise `--stall-timeout`; the pool's own guidance is that pinning names a member deliberately and does not widen the allow-list. Tracked in #3361, where the root cause is left unstated and the options are weighed.

pool.why: Re-admitted 2026-09-30 on the bar this file requires, not renamed in. NaN retired its predecessor mimo-v2.5 that day: it hung, then answered 401 'This API key does not have access to the requested model' (AI-045, #1763). mimo-v2.5 had been admitted 2026-08-20 on a planted-defect test, and the successor was given the same one: the `((count++))` exit-status-1 case under `set -e` from this repo's prohibited-pattern table. mimo-v2.6-flash found it in 21 s and 772 completion tokens, named a failing input (count=0), and gave the fix (`count=$((count + 1))`). deepseek-v4-flash, run on the same prompt, found the same defect in 9 s. That is agreement on one planted defect, not a quality ranking, and it is stated as that. It stays a SECOND fallback, after the provider-diverse one, because provider diversity remains the stronger property. Profile: 1M context, reasoning chain, which is this pool's line against qwen3.6 and gemma4 at 262K.
pool.operational_note: Reasoning models here emit reasoning_content BEFORE content. Under-provisioning max_tokens returns an empty body with finish_reason=length and no error — the same shape as a review that silently did not happen (lesson 213). Provision generously and check finish_reason. NaN recommends max_tokens >= 300 for this model and publishes a per-model concurrency limit of 5. Measured in PR-Agent 2026-10-09 to 11-05 (#2216): 25% of attempts ended empty at NaN's reasoning-only ceiling (60,000 characters or 420 s, ai/nan/README.md), which no cap of ours moves and which `reasoning_effort` does not shorten for this model; mean 379 s of a NaN slot per draw against 127 s for deepseek and 35 s for glm, so at weight 27 it held 77% of the pool's NaN slot time, and it was the only member NaN answered 429. Hence weight 12: its addressed findings per review (about 0.46) match deepseek's, which takes the share it gives up.

pool.why: Admitted 2026-08-29 by owner decision (HARNESS-093, #1370) to spread reviews across NaN's PER-MODEL concurrency buckets and exercise more than one model on the gate. What IS established: reasoning-class by profile — pi-nan-provider's snapshot marks glm5.3-flash reasoning: true with a 1M context, the line this pool draws (tests/pi-nan-package.bats holds it). What is NOT established: a calibration against a review of known outcome (e.g. CLI-050 round 1's real Major); recorded here so nobody reads this entry as measured equivalence to deepseek. Drawn at random like every member; --reviewer names it deliberately.

Admitted 2026-08-29 by owner decision (HARNESS-093, #1370) to spread reviews across NaN's per-model concurrency buckets and exercise more than one model on the gate. What IS established: reasoning-class by profile — pi-nan-provider's snapshot marks qwen3.8-flash reasoning: true, and ai/pi/models.json corrects its stale native-window snapshot to NaN's served 1,048,576-token window (tests/pi-nan-package.bats holds the effective values). What is NOT established: a calibration against a review of known outcome (e.g. CLI-050 round 1's real Major); recorded here so nobody reads this entry as measured equivalence to deepseek. Drawn at random like every member; --reviewer names it deliberately.

Admitted 2026-10-09 by owner decision (#1923, amendment B). In the adversarial review it signs only as a FALLBACK, with a classified reason (rate limit, quota, provider error, timeout, content filter, empty answer) when the NaN first signers failed; it never signs first by draw. In PR-Agent it is drawn at weight 50, half of reviews, to offload NaN, whose shared concurrency is the scarcer resource (owner, 2026-11-05, #2216; 35 from 2026-10-09). Measured 2026-10-09 to 11-05 (#2216, 456 published reviews): mean 40.7K tokens in and 5.7K out, about $0.035 a review at the rates above the price step and less below it; median 18 s from request to publish; 1.0% of attempts empty at `length` since effort dropped to medium (#2459, against 5 of 11 at high). Its findings are the most numerous (3.6 a review) and the least often addressed: 12% of line-anchored findings had their lines changed before the next review that dropped them, against 24-35% for the NaN members, about 0.31 addressed a review against 0.46 for deepseek and mimo. Reasoning-class by profile (adaptive thinking). Effort is medium, not high: at high, thinking spent the 32,000-token output cap on large diffs and the answer came back empty in 5 of 11 runs (#2458).

Admitted 2026-10-09 by owner decision (#1923, amendment B) as the quality tier, placed where it pays: the SECOND signature of a `risk: high` spec (about 8 a month, about $1.60 each agentic), and in PR-Agent the first review of a PR past `pr_agent_risk` (about 3% of PRs at 1500 changed lines, about $0.37 each, measured). Never drawn at random in either flow: at 15x Haiku's PR-Agent price a uniform share would spend the month's budget in a week. No calibration yet; #2215 and #2216 measure it.

pr_agent_risk.label: deep-review
pr_agent_risk.$comment: A PR reviews first on the `route: risk` member when its additions plus deletions reach min_changed_lines, or it carries the label. Set to 1500 by owner decision 2026-10-09: the first live Sonnet review cost $0.37, not $0.13, because a PR this large fills the prompt cap, and over the last 395 merged PRs 9.1% reach 900 lines, 4.8% reach 1200 and 3.0% reach 1500. At 1500 the route costs about $28 of the $60-65 month. A path-based predicate matched 14-35% and was rejected as too costly. Measured 2026-10-09 to 11-05 (#2216): the route took 1.9% of drawn reviews, not 3%, at a mean of $0.22 (60.9K tokens in), about $8 a month.
